# Harness Compatibility Baseline

`agent_spec_legacy_context_window.json` is a fixed, fictional AgentSpec covering native definition fields and Harness extensions, including the historical `model_characteristics.context_window` input. It is deliberately not regenerated by tests. The `$schema` value is metadata; tests do not fetch it.

The companion `test_agent_spec_compatibility.py` checks semantic values, canonical serialization, native/Harness capability construction, and an offline run followed by JSON state restoration and a rebuilt-agent continuation. Existing Harness CI discovers this test with the Linux package suite; no additional workflow, release matrix, credentials, or schema-version change is needed.

| Coverage                                                                  | Boundary                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Model identity, instructions, metadata, schemas, retries and settings     | Native AgentSpec values retained by Harness                          |
| System prompts, cold-start policy, usage limits and model characteristics | Harness-owned definition inputs                                      |
| Legacy context-window spelling                                            | Read compatibility with canonical current output                     |
| Four representative declarative capabilities                              | Native shorthand/standard forms and first-party Harness registration |
| Local model run and rebuilt-agent continuation                            | Definition consumption and current state save/restore                |

The state round trip is not a claim that every historical HarnessState or old package version is supported. UI configuration trees, snapshot digest selection, and WebUI startup belong to the small UI integration regression, not this Harness baseline. Provider authentication, external tools, and hosted services retain their own tests.

Changes to established inputs require advance human agreement and explicit PR review under [CONTRIBUTING.md](/CONTRIBUTING.md#compatibility-baselines). Prefer adding a case over replacing accepted input. The initial fixture may be refined within the human-authorized task that establishes it; once accepted, do not rewrite it to follow an internal rename.
